ows:ServiceIdentification.ows:Title: EFFIS - OGC/WFS Test Service
ows:ServiceIdentification.ows:Abstract: The European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) supports the services in charge of the protection of forests against fires in the EU countries and provides the European Commission services and the European Parliament with updated and reliable information on wildland fires in Europe.

FeatureType.Name: ms:all.hs
FeatureType.Title: all.hs
FeatureType.Abstract: The layer aggregates fire‑related thermal‑anomaly (hotspot) detections from the MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP/NOAA‑20) sensors as used in the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS). Each point represents a cloud‑masked observation of active fire, including latitude, longitude, detection confidence and estimated radiative power. MODIS provides ~1 km resolution with up to four daily passes, while VIIRS delivers 375 m resolution with up to fourteen daily passes, ensuring comprehensive and near‑real‑time coverage of fires of all sizes across the EU. The combined catalogue supports fire‑danger mapping, early‑warning bulletins and operational response within the EFFIS framework.

FeatureType.Name: ms:viirs.hs
FeatureType.Title: viirs.hs
FeatureType.Abstract: The layer shows VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) thermal‑anomaly (hotspot) detections used within the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS). Each feature represents a cloud‑masked fire‑related radiance observation, providing the geographic location, detection confidence and estimated radiative power of active fires. The product is generated from near‑real‑time observations of the Suomi NPP satellites at a spatial resolution of approximately 375 m, with up to 14 observations per day, and is integrated into EFFIS fire‑danger maps and daily fire‑information bulletins to support early warning, risk assessment and operational response across the EU.

FeatureType.Name: ms:noaa.hs
FeatureType.Title: noaa.hs
FeatureType.Abstract: The layer shows VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) thermal‑anomaly (hotspot) detections used within the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS). Each feature represents a cloud‑masked fire‑related radiance observation, providing the geographic location, detection confidence and estimated radiative power of active fires. The product is generated from near‑real‑time observations of the NOAA‑20 satellites at a spatial resolution of approximately 375 m, with up to 14 observations per day, and is integrated into EFFIS fire‑danger maps and daily fire‑information bulletins to support early warning, risk assessment and operational response across the EU.

FeatureType.Name: ms:modis.hs
FeatureType.Title: modis.hs
FeatureType.Abstract: MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) hotspot detections represent cloud‑masked thermal‑anomaly observations used within the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS). Each record provides the geographic position, detection confidence and estimated radiative power of active fires, derived from the Terra and Aqua satellites at a spatial resolution of approximately 1 km (1 km fire‑related band). The product delivers near‑real‑time observations with up to four passes per day, supporting fire‑risk assessment, early‑warning mapping and operational response across the EU.
